TestName: Login screen displays username and password fields
TestSteps: 1. Open client app. 2. Observe login screen.
ExpectedResult: Username and password fields are visible and clearly labeled.

TestName: Client establishes TCP connection before authentication commands
Preconditions: Client app is launched and server is available
TestSteps: 1. Start server. 2. Start client. 3. Attempt login or command flow.
ExpectedResult: Client opens TCP connection before sending authentication or control commands.

TestName: Client sends device control command using predefined packet format
Preconditions: User is logged in and client can send commands
TestSteps: 1. Open controllable room. 2. Trigger device ON or OFF command.
ExpectedResult: Client constructs and sends a correctly formatted control packet.

TestName: Client shows success or failure response after command
Preconditions: User is logged in and server response can be observed
TestSteps: 1. Send a valid or invalid command. 2. Observe client feedback.
ExpectedResult: Clear success or failure message is shown after the command completes.

TestName: Logout returns user to login screen
TestSteps: 1. Click logout or disconnect action.
ExpectedResult: Session ends and login screen is shown.

TestName: Connection lost message is shown and user can retry
TestSteps: 1. Disconnect server unexpectedly. 2. Observe client behavior. 3. Try reconnecting.
ExpectedResult: Client shows a connection lost message and allows retry without restart.

TestName: Last server IP and port are remembered on next launch
Preconditions: Client supports IP and port settings
TestSteps: 1. Enter server IP and port. 2. Close client. 3. Relaunch client.
ExpectedResult: Last used server IP and port are auto-filled.

TestName: Server listens for incoming TCP client connections
TestSteps: 1. Start server. 2. Attempt client connection.
ExpectedResult: Server accepts client session before processing requests.

TestName: Server authenticates valid credentials before non-authentication commands
TestSteps: 1. Submit valid credentials. 2. Observe session state.
ExpectedResult: Authenticated session is created for valid credentials.

TestName: Server implements LOCKED HOME AWAY and MAINTENANCE states
TestSteps: 1. Create state machine. 2. Inspect states and transitions.
ExpectedResult: Operational states exist and can be used by the server.

TestName: Server changes operational state only on valid authenticated SET_MODE
Preconditions: Request handler and authenticated session are available
TestSteps: 1. Try SET_MODE without auth. 2. Try SET_MODE with auth.
ExpectedResult: SET_MODE only succeeds when valid and authenticated.

TestName: Server processes device control commands and returns acknowledgment
Preconditions: Device manager and request handler are available
TestSteps: 1. Send device control command. 2. Observe result and acknowledgment.
ExpectedResult: Device command is processed and success or failure is returned.

TestName: Server rejects commands not allowed in current state
Preconditions: State machine and request handler are available
TestSteps: 1. Enter restricted state. 2. Attempt restricted command.
ExpectedResult: Command is rejected with error response and state does not change.

TestName: Server sends JPEG image of at least 1 MB on valid request
Preconditions: Server has valid image source file
TestSteps: 1. Send valid image request to server. 2. Measure returned payload.
ExpectedResult: Server returns valid JPEG data of at least 1 MB.

TestName: Server logs every transmitted and received packet
TestSteps: 1. Perform network actions. 2. Inspect server log file.
ExpectedResult: Each packet event is logged with required metadata.

TestName: Server supports reconnect after client disconnect without restart
TestSteps: 1. Connect client. 2. Disconnect client. 3. Reconnect client without restarting server.
ExpectedResult: Server accepts reconnection successfully.

TestName: Server maintains and returns current device status list
Preconditions: Device manager and request handler are available
TestSteps: 1. Change device states. 2. Request status list.
ExpectedResult: Current device statuses are returned correctly.

TestName: State machine initializes in LOCKED and transitions to HOME after successful authentication
TestSteps: 1. Create state machine. 2. Validate initial state. 3. Transition on successful auth path.
ExpectedResult: Initial state is LOCKED and valid transition to HOME is supported.

TestName: State machine rejects device commands in LOCKED and MAINTENANCE
Preconditions: Authenticated session and request handler are available
TestSteps: 1. Enter LOCKED or MAINTENANCE. 2. Attempt device command.
ExpectedResult: Restricted commands are rejected.

TestName: State machine transitions from HOME to AWAY after inactivity timeout
TestSteps: 1. Enter HOME. 2. Wait for inactivity timeout.
ExpectedResult: System transitions automatically to AWAY after timeout.

TestName: State machine enters Safe Mode after repeated failed authentication attempts
TestSteps: 1. Submit multiple failed logins in short period.
ExpectedResult: System transitions to LOCKED safe mode as specified.

TestName: Packet uses fixed header variable body and 2-byte tail
TestSteps: 1. Serialize packet with payload. 2. Inspect size and layout.
ExpectedResult: Serialized packet contains header body and 2-byte tail.

TestName: Packet supports variable-length payload through dynamic storage
TestSteps: 1. Set payloads of different sizes including empty and non-empty.
ExpectedResult: Packet handles variable-length payloads correctly.

TestName: Packet includes status code in responses
TestSteps: 1. Create packet with status code. 2. Serialize and deserialize.
ExpectedResult: Status code field is preserved correctly.

TestName: Packet contains fixed magic number in header
TestSteps: 1. Create and validate packet. 2. Try invalid magic packet.
ExpectedResult: Valid packets contain magic number and invalid magic is rejected.

TestName: Packet checksum detects corruption
TestSteps: 1. Corrupt serialized packet. 2. Attempt deserialization.
ExpectedResult: Corrupted packet fails validation.

TestName: Packet version field supports compatibility checks
TestSteps: 1. Inspect default version. 2. Attempt invalid version packet.
ExpectedResult: Valid version is set by default and invalid version is rejected.

TestName: Communication occurs over TCP/IP protocol
TestSteps: 1. Establish socket pair. 2. Send and receive bytes.
ExpectedResult: Reliable ordered communication occurs over TCP sockets.

TestName: Client times out after 5 seconds without ACK
Preconditions: ACK timeout handling is implemented in client
TestSteps: 1. Send command without server ACK. 2. Measure client timeout behavior.
ExpectedResult: Client reports communication failure after 5 seconds.

TestName: Server keeps persistent connection open until explicit disconnect
Preconditions: Server is running and persistent session handling is implemented
TestSteps: 1. Connect client. 2. Send multiple commands. 3. Verify socket remains open until disconnect.
ExpectedResult: Connection persists until explicit disconnect command or shutdown.

TestName: Server sends transfers greater than 1 MB in 4 KB chunks
TestSteps: 1. Request image larger than 1 MB. 2. Inspect chunk sizes during transmission.
ExpectedResult: Large transfer is sent in sequential 4 KB chunks.

TestName: Client attempts auto-reconnect three times before returning to login
TestSteps: 1. Disconnect server. 2. Observe client reconnect attempts.
ExpectedResult: Client retries three times then returns to login screen.

TestName: Client and server log transmitted and received packets
TestSteps: 1. Send and receive packets. 2. Inspect logs.
ExpectedResult: Both applications record TX and RX packet activity.

TestName: Logs contain timestamp direction command type and data length
TestSteps: 1. Generate packet traffic. 2. Inspect log entries.
ExpectedResult: Each log line includes required metadata fields.

TestName: Logs are stored in designated log directory
TestSteps: 1. Generate logs. 2. Inspect application log directory.
ExpectedResult: Logs are saved to designated log folder under application path.

TestName: Applications show error if log file operation fails
TestSteps: 1. Block log file access. 2. Trigger logging operation.
ExpectedResult: Application shows clear log failure message.

TestName: New log file is created for each session
Preconditions: Multiple application sessions can be started
TestSteps: 1. Start and stop application multiple times. 2. Inspect generated log files.
ExpectedResult: A new session log file is created each time.

TestName: Log includes summary of command or device action
TestSteps: 1. Send representative commands. 2. Inspect log contents.
ExpectedResult: Logs include readable action summary for troubleshooting.

TestName: Current smart home mode is clearly visible to the user
Preconditions: Participant is logged into client app
TestSteps: 1. Ask participant to identify current system mode.
ExpectedResult: Participant can quickly locate and understand current mode display.

TestName: Available smart home device status is clearly displayed
Preconditions: Participant is logged into client app
TestSteps: 1. Ask participant to identify device states in a room.
ExpectedResult: Participant can understand which devices are on off or otherwise active.

TestName: Controls for device and mode changes are clearly labeled
Preconditions: Participant is logged into client app
TestSteps: 1. Ask participant to change a mode or device state without help.
ExpectedResult: Participant can identify the correct controls without confusion.

TestName: Successful command completion shows clear confirmation
Preconditions: Participant is logged into client app
TestSteps: 1. Ask participant to perform successful command. 2. Observe whether confirmation is noticed.
ExpectedResult: Participant sees and understands the success feedback.

TestName: Failed command shows clear error feedback
Preconditions: Participant is logged in or at login screen
TestSteps: 1. Trigger a failing action. 2. Ask participant what happened.
ExpectedResult: Participant understands the failure and possible next action.

TestName: Device controls and status information are organized logically
Preconditions: Participant is logged into client app
TestSteps: 1. Ask participant to locate related controls and statuses. 2. Observe navigation and hesitation.
ExpectedResult: Layout feels logical and related items are grouped understandably.

TestName: TCP handshake is established before data exchange
TestSteps: 1. Start server. 2. Start client. 3. Observe initial connection setup.
ExpectedResult: TCP handshake completes before packets are exchanged.

TestName: Client and server interpret synchronized command IDs consistently
Preconditions: Client and server packet handling are available
TestSteps: 1. Send representative commands. 2. Verify receiver interprets the intended command.
ExpectedResult: Both sides interpret command IDs consistently.

TestName: Server sends ACK packet for every received control command
TestSteps: 1. Send control command from client. 2. Observe server response.
ExpectedResult: ACK is returned for each received control command.

TestName: Unexpected socket closure notifies client and is logged by server
TestSteps: 1. Disconnect socket unexpectedly. 2. Observe client and server behavior.
ExpectedResult: Client shows connection error and server logs the event.

TestName: Large JPEG transfer is fragmented and reassembled correctly
Preconditions: Valid image transfer feature is implemented
TestSteps: 1. Request image larger than 1 MB. 2. Observe server transfer and client display.
ExpectedResult: Image is transferred in fragments and correctly reassembled for display.

TestName: Heartbeat or keep-alive maintains idle connection
TestSteps: 1. Leave client-server connection idle for longer than 30 seconds. 2. Observe keep-alive behavior.
ExpectedResult: Heartbeat packets maintain active connection during idle period.

TestName: Server broadcasts device state update without prior request
TestSteps: 1. Change device state on server side. 2. Observe whether client receives unsolicited update.
ExpectedResult: Client receives broadcast status update automatically.

TestName: Full workflow from startup to logout succeeds
Preconditions: Client and server build successfully and can run
TestSteps: 1. Start server. 2. Start client. 3. Log in. 4. Navigate rooms. 5. Control device. 6. Log out.
ExpectedResult: All major operations complete successfully end-to-end.

TestName: Full image workflow transfers and displays valid snapshot
Preconditions: Server has valid snapshot file and client can display images
TestSteps: 1. Start server. 2. Start client. 3. Log in. 4. Open Garage. 5. Request snapshot.
ExpectedResult: Snapshot is transferred and displayed correctly end-to-end.

TestName: Invalid login prevents dashboard access and allows retry
TestSteps: 1. Attempt invalid login. 2. Observe failure. 3. Retry with valid credentials.
ExpectedResult: Access is denied on failure and valid retry works cleanly.

TestName: Server offline scenario is handled gracefully
Preconditions: Client is built and server is offline
TestSteps: 1. Launch client. 2. Attempt server-dependent action.
ExpectedResult: Client remains stable and presents meaningful connection error.

TestName: State restrictions are enforced across complete system
Preconditions: Client and server are connected and user is authenticated
TestSteps: 1. Put system in restricted state. 2. Attempt restricted device command from client.
ExpectedResult: Command is blocked and feedback is shown correctly end-to-end.
